text:
Ravi K: Heads-up: Sales asked for a single-pane "unit-econ" card that shows model cost + "prefetch pool amortization" per tenant. They want to reconcile invoices when prefetch is shared across many customers.

Marta S: Can you define "prefetch pool amortization" precisely? Do you want per-tenant allocated USD, or a token-equivalent plus allocation factor?

Ravi K: Prefer USD so it's directly comparable to invoices. But also show token-equivalent on hover. The tricky part is how we split shared prefetch credits when multiple tenants hit the same prefetch.

Chris D: Telemetry constraints: we currently attribute prefetch writes to a fingerprint key but not to tenant_id until request-time. To compute USD allocation we need either (A) emit attribution with tenant_id at time of prefetch (high cardinality) or (B) run a join in rollups that maps prefetch id -> list of tenants that consumed it within window. Option B is heavier but avoids increasing event cardinality.

Nina: Ops perspective: Option B will need us to store prefetch metadata (prefetch_id, model_hash, created_at) for 7 days and then materialize consumption joins. Storage + join cost ~ moderate. We can compress with bloom filters per-hour to approximate membership.

Marta S: UX idea: show two numbers side-by-side: "Allocated prefetch (USD)" and "Allocation method (pro-rated | naive-equal | request-weighted)" with a dropdown so users can compare. That avoids pinning a single legal method while Sales experiments with reconciliations.

Ravi K: Nice. For initial rollout default to request-weighted (i.e., weight by tokens_consumed_by_tenant on the prefetched item in the amortization window).

Chris D: Implementation sketch: emit two rollups hourly: 
```
# 1) prefetch_meta_hourly: prefetch_id, model_hash, tokens_total, created_hour
# 2) consumption_hourly: prefetch_id, tenant_id, tokens_consumed
```
Then allocation job joins them and computes tenant_alloc_usd = tokens_consumed / tokens_total * prefetch_cost_usd. We'll need to cap at tokens_total to avoid double-counting.

Nina: Sampling note: to control cardinality we can sample consumption events at 2% and then scale up in the join. Add a confidence score on the card indicating sampling variance.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled job "prefetch-allocation-rollup" planned for 2026-04-02 04:00 UTC (staging).

Marta S: For the console card layout I propose: left column = model name + sparkline (tokens saved), center = net model cost (USD), right = prefetch allocated USD (with small "i" tooltip), below = combo control to switch allocation method and toggle raw tokens view. Include a warning stripe when allocation confidence < 80%.

Chris D: Edge-case: deduped prefetches (same fingerprint) created across windows — join must coalesce by fingerprint+model_hash. Also account for evicted prefetches where consumption happens after eviction window; mark as "late consumption" and attribute to a fallback (unallocated bucket).

Ravi K: Legal/sales will want an exportable CSV for an invoice reconciliation flow. Can we add an export button that hits the rollup API and returns per-tenant lines for a given billing period?

Nina: Yes, the rollup service can expose /v1/prefetch_allocations?start=...&end=...&method=request_weighted and produce per-tenant rows. We'll need RBAC so only billing/sales can call it.

product-bot: reminder: add "prefetch_allocation_method" to product telemetry schema v1.2 when rolling out.

Marta S: I'll prototype the card in Figma and show a compact and expanded view. Ravi, can you get sample CSV use cases from Sales so we shape the export columns?

Ravi K: On it. I'll collect 3 example customers and share by EOD. Thanks team :raised_hands:
